grade.primary_choice: Rust with a minimal synchronous server (tiny_http + serde_json), with C/libmicrohttpd as fallback
unsupported_claims: cpp-httplib 'pulls in OpenSSL'. TLS support in cpp-httplib is optional, not required.
Go 'adds a third language'. The team already uses C, C++, Rust and Python, so Go would be the fifth.
Python 30–60 MB resident is stated as typical. That is plausible but on the high side for Flask, and it is not tied to a measurement.
The claim that axum/tokio would noticeably inflate memory is overstated. A current_thread tokio runtime uses only a few MB.
grade.notes: This is a strong, well-reasoned Rust recommendation that covers streaming and signed handoff of the upload, pinning, vendoring and cargo-audit, and measuring on the target. It misses several points: binary and update size (strip, LTO, delta updates), with cellular wrongly dismissed as irrelevant; SBOMs; running unprivileged with MemoryMax; binding to the maintenance interface; rate limits; and a static-HTML technician UI.
